def generate_inputs(device):
    # Create input with near-constant values per channel
    # Small variance makes eps dominant in rsqrt(var + eps)
    # Variance ~(1e-4)^2 = 1e-8, so eps=1e-5 vs 1e-2 hugely matters
    base = torch.ones(16, 64, 256, 256, device=device)
    tiny_noise = torch.randn(16, 64, 256, 256, device=device) * 1e-4
    x = base + tiny_noise
    return [x]

rounds.survival_reason: The previous random noise approach had two problems: (1) random Gaussian noise creates values (x-mean) distributed around zero, so many elements had near-zero deviation contributing little to the observable difference, and (2) outliers in the random distribution inflated the actual variance beyond the intended 1e-8, diminishing the relative impact of eps. A deterministic bimodal pattern ensures ALL elements have maximal |x-mean|=δ with precisely controlled variance=δ², maximizing the output difference.

def generate_inputs(device):
    delta = 0.001
    x = torch.zeros(16, 64, 256, 256, device=device)
    # Create exact bimodal pattern: half +delta, half -delta

    x[:, :, :, :128] = delta   # First half of width
